13:1.headline: Why 'old' needs 'advanced in days' beside it
13:1.body: Metzudat David says זקן, old, describes what people see: white hair and a wrinkled face. Those can come early. So the verse adds 'advanced in days' to say Joshua was truly old in years.

sources.quote: זקן יאמר לשון בני אדם המוחש, הנראה באדם מלובן השער והקמטת הפנים, ולפעמים מקדים לבוא בלא עת
sources.says: Metzudat David says 'old' speaks of visible signs like white hair and wrinkles, which sometimes come too early, so 'advanced in days' is added.

13:6.headline: 'Make it fall': divide even unconquered land by lot
13:6.body: הפלה means 'make it fall', that is, cast the lot. Rashi and Metzudat David say Joshua must divide the land now, even the parts not yet taken. Each tribe will later conquer what fell to it.

sources.quote: וְיִכְבּוֹשׁ לְאַחַר זְמָן כָּל שֵׁבֶט וְשֵׁבֶט מַה שֶּׁנָּפַל בְּגוֹרָלוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says each tribe will later conquer what fell to it by lot.

sources.quote: הטל הגורל ביניהם על מה שכבר כבשו ועל מה שלא כבשו עדיין
sources.says: Metzudat David says Joshua should cast lots for what was conquered and what was not yet conquered.

13:6.headline: Not 'inheritance' by conquest but land passed down to grandchildren
13:6.body: Malbim says ירושה and נחלה are different. ירושה is land moving from one owner to another. נחלה is what a family hands down. This land was not yet taken, so the verse can only call it נחלה.

sources.quote: ירושה מציין הורקת הרשות, שיוצא מרשות זה לרשות אחר, ונחלה מציין מה שמנחיל בני בנים
sources.says: Malbim says ירושה means ownership passing to another, and נחלה means what one passes on to one's grandchildren.

13:12.headline: Og was left over from the giants struck in Abraham's day
13:12.body: The verse calls Og a remnant of the Rephaim. Rashi says these are the Rephaim that Chedorlaomer and his allies struck in Genesis 14. Og survived that war.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָרַג כְּדָרְלָעֹמֶר וְהַמְּלָכִים אֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says these are the Rephaim killed by Chedorlaomer and the kings with him, as in Genesis 14:5.

13:22.headline: Killed 'onto their slain': the midrash of the falling sorcerers
13:22.body: Radak says אל חלליהם plainly means 'with their slain'. He also cites a midrash. Balaam and the kings of Midian flew in the air by sorcery, and fell onto their dead when Pinchas showed them the priest's gold plate.

sources.quote: שהיו מלכי מדין עושים כשפים עם בלעם ובורחים מפני חרב ישראל ופורחין באויר
sources.says: Radak cites a midrash that the kings of Midian used sorcery with Balaam and flew in the air to escape Israel's sword.

sources.quote: ולא היה יכול להציל עצמו בקסמיו
sources.says: Metzudat David says Balaam died with the other slain and could not save himself with his magic.

13:28.headline: Not 'courtyards' but open villages around the walled towns
13:28.body: חצר usually means a courtyard. Rashi and Metzudat Zion say here it means villages without walls, around the walled cities.

sources.quote: וְחַצְרֵיהֶם עָרֵי הַפְּרָזִי בְּלֹא חוֹמָה
sources.says: Rashi says these are open towns without a wall.

sources.quote: עיירות פרוזות מבלי חומה, העומדים סביב עיר חומה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they are unwalled villages standing around a walled city.

14:4.headline: The city's outskirts are called 'driven out' places
14:4.body: Metzudat Zion says מגרשיהם are the buildings right beside a city, outside its wall. They are called this as if they were driven out of the city.

sources.quote: ומגרשיהם. הם הבנינים הסמוכים להעיר, מחוץ לחומה, וכאלו נגרשו ממנה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says מגרשיהם are the buildings next to the city, outside the wall, as if driven out of it.

14:7.headline: 'As in my heart' also means 'not as in my mouth'
14:7.body: Rashi adds the other half of the sentence: not as with his mouth. On the road Caleb had gone along with the other spies in words, out of fear, but he told Moses what he really thought. Radak says he agreed with them so they would not kill him.

sources.quote: כַּאֲשֶׁר עִם לְבָבִי וְלֹא כַּאֲשֶׁר עִם פִּי, שֶׁהַמְרַגְּלִים הָיוּ בְּעֵצָה אַחַת
sources.says: Rashi says 'as with my heart' means 'and not as with my mouth', because the spies were of one counsel.

sources.quote: היה מסכים עמהם בדברים כדי שלא יהרגוהו
sources.says: Radak says Caleb agreed with the spies in words so they would not kill him.

sources.quote: כי בפיו היה בעצה אחת עם יתר המרגלים, כי פחד מהם
sources.says: Metzudat David says that with his mouth Caleb was of one counsel with the other spies, because he feared them.

14:8.headline: An odd spelling of 'made melt', with an Aramaic-style ending
14:8.body: The ending with yod and vav is not the usual Hebrew plural. Radak says it matches Aramaic, as in אשתיו חמרא. Malbim agrees and gives the root as מסה.

sources.quote: שלא כמנהג וי"ו הרבים בלשון הקדש אבל בלשון ארמי יבא כמו כן אשתיו חמרא
sources.says: Radak says this is not the usual Hebrew plural ending, but it appears in Aramaic, as in אשתיו חמרא.

sources.quote: ומלת המסיו בא על משקל הארמי אתיו חמרא
sources.says: Malbim says המסיו follows the Aramaic pattern, like אתיו חמרא.

14:9.headline: 'If not' opens an oath, and the threat is left unsaid
14:9.body: Metzudat David says אם לא is the wording of an oath. It means 'if this does not happen, let such and such punishment come', but the punishment is never spoken. He compares Job 1:11.

sources.quote: הוא ענין לשון שבועה, כאלו אמר אם לא יהיה הדבר הזה אזי יהיה עונשו כך וכך, וגזם ולא אמר
sources.says: Metzudat David says אם לא is the language of an oath, as if the punishment were named, but it is left out.

14:9.headline: 'The land your foot trod' is Hebron, and only Caleb went there
14:9.body: Radak says this land is Hebron. Numbers says 'he came' to Hebron, one person, because the other spies were afraid of the giants. Metzudat Zion says דרכה means stepped, from the word for a way.

sources.quote: זו היא חברון שנאמר ויבא עד חברון ולא אמר ויבאו לפי שהמרגלים האחרים היו יראים לבא שם מפני הענקים
sources.says: Radak says the land is Hebron, and Numbers says 'he came', not 'they came', since the other spies feared the giants there.

sources.quote: דרכה. צעדה, והוא מלשון דרך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says דרכה means 'stepped' and comes from the word דרך.

14:10.headline: Forty-five years hide a count: the conquest took seven years
14:10.body: Rashi and Radak work out the number. The spies went out in the second year, so 38 years were left in the wilderness. Add 7 years of conquering and you reach 45.

sources.quote: שֶׁהֲרֵי בַּשָּׁנָה הַשֵּׁנִית שָׁלַח משֶׁה הַמְרַגְּלִים, נִשְׁאֲרוּ שְׁלשִׁים וּשְׁמֹנֶה שֶׁהָלְכוּ בַּמִּדְבָּר וְשֶׁבַע שֶׁכָּבְשׁוּ
sources.says: Rashi says Moses sent the spies in the second year, so 38 years remained in the wilderness, and 7 more were spent conquering.

sources.quote: והנה נשארו להם במדבר שלשים ושמנה שנה ושבע שכבשו הנה ארבעים וחמש
sources.says: Radak gives the same sum: 38 in the wilderness and 7 of conquest make 45.

14:11.headline: Caleb puts 'then' and 'now' in an odd order
14:11.body: Two comparing letters כ sit side by side. Radak says this makes the comparison run both ways, so his strength then and now are exactly equal. Malbim says normal grammar would put it the other way round, and explains that no one knew Caleb's strength back then until he later fought.

sources.quote: וכן כחי עתה ככחי אז וכחי אז ככחי עתה הכל בשוה
sources.says: Radak says 'my strength now like my strength then' and the reverse are all equal.

sources.quote: אבל כפי משפט הלשון היה ראוי להיות בהיפך ככחי עתה ככחי אז
sources.says: Malbim says normal grammar would have put it the other way, 'like my strength now, like my strength then'.

14:12.headline: Caleb's אותי means 'with me', not just 'me'
14:12.body: אותי usually marks 'me' as the object. Radak and Metzudat Zion read it here as 'with me', as in ואדברה אותך, 'and I will speak with you'. Malbim says the expected spelling is אתי.

sources.quote: ה' אותי. כמו עמי וכן ואדברה אותך והדומים להם
sources.says: Radak says אותי here is like עמי, 'with me', as in ואדברה אותך.

sources.quote: אותי. עמי, אף כי הוא בחול״ם, וכן (יחזקאל ב א) ואדבר אותך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says אותי means 'with me' although it is pointed with a cholam, as in Ezekiel 2:1.

sources.quote: אולי ה' אותי. היו ראוי אתי
sources.says: Malbim says the expected form here would be אתי.

14:13.headline: Joshua gave Caleb 'Hebron', but not the city itself
14:13.body: Radak says 'Hebron' here means the city's fields and villages. The city itself was a city of refuge, and it belonged to the priests.

sources.quote: פירוש שדה העיר וחצריה כי העיר עצמה היתה מקלט
sources.says: Radak says it means the city's field and villages, since the city itself was a city of refuge.

sources.quote: שדה העיר וחצריה, אבל העיר עצמה היתה עיר מקלט
sources.says: Metzudat David says the same: the field and villages, while the city was a city of refuge.

14:15.headline: Kiryat Arba: named for a giant, or for 'four'?
14:15.body: Rashi says Arba was the name of the father of Achiman, Sheshai and Talmai. He also gives another reading: the town is named for the father and his three sons, four in all. Radak also says Arba was the giant's name.

sources.quote: אֲבִיהֶם שֶׁל אֲחִימָן שֵׁשַׁי וְתַלְמַי, אַרְבַּע הָיָה שְׁמוֹ. דָּבָר אַחֵר: עַל שֵׁם הָאָב וּשְׁלשָׁה בָּנִים
sources.says: Rashi says Arba was the father's name, and another reading is that the name counts the father and three sons.

sources.quote: ארבע הוא שם הענק והוא האדם הגדול בענקים
sources.says: Radak says Arba is the name of the giant, the great man among the Anakim.

14:15.headline: Who is 'the great man among the Anakim'? Maybe Abraham
14:15.body: Rashi first reads it as Arba, the father of the Anakim. A midrash he quotes reads it as Abraham. Because the people of Hebron honored him, the land had forty years without war while Israel was in the wilderness.

sources.quote: הָאָדָם הַגָּדוֹל בָּעֲנָקִים הוּא אֲבִיהֶם שֶׁל אֲחִימָן שֵׁשַׁי וְתַלְמַי
sources.says: Rashi says the great man among the Anakim is the father of Achiman, Sheshai and Talmai.

sources.quote: הָאָדָם הַגָּדוֹל בָּעֲנָקִים הוּא אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ, הוּא שֶׁגָּרַם לָהֶם שֶׁהָאָרֶץ שָׁקְטָה מִמִּלְחָמָה אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה
sources.says: A midrash Rashi quotes says the great man is Abraham, who caused the land to be quiet from war for forty years.

sources.quote: גם למול ענקים היה נחשב לגדול וגבה הקומה
sources.says: Metzudat David says that even next to the Anakim he was counted great and tall.

15:2.headline: The 'tongue' is a strip of sea, or a tongue of rock
15:2.body: לשון means tongue. Metzudat Zion says it is the tip of the sea, stretched out like a tongue, while Targum Jonathan, as Radak notes, reads it as a rock that juts south.

sources.quote: ראש הים המשוך כלשון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the tongue is the head of the sea, drawn out like a tongue.

sources.quote: ויונתן תרגם כיפא דמיתפני לדרומא ר״ל לשון סלע
sources.says: Radak says it is a tongue of the sea, and notes that Targum Jonathan renders it as a rock turning south, a tongue of rock.

15:7.headline: Ein Rogel is the washers' spring, named for treading feet
15:7.body: רגל means foot. Rashi and Radak say a washer was called rogel because he scrubs clothes with his feet, so this was the spring where clothes were washed.

sources.quote: וְקוֹרֵא אֶת הַכּוֹבֵס רוֹגֵל, עַל שֵׁם שֶׁבּוֹעֵט אֶת בִּגְדֵי הַצֶּמֶר בְּרַגְלָיו
sources.says: Rashi says it is the washers' spring, and a washer is called rogel because he kicks the wool clothes with his feet.

sources.quote: ונקרא הכובס רוגל לפי שמשפשף הבגדים ברגליו בעת שמכבסם
sources.says: Radak says the washer is called rogel because he rubs the clothes with his feet while washing them.

15:9.headline: The border curves around, like a line drawn with a compass
15:9.body: ותאר is a rare verb. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it from Isaiah's 'he marks it out with a compass', so the border here bends around a place.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן וְנָסַב בְּעוֹגֶל, כְּמוֹ (ישעיהו מד יג): וּבַמְּחוּגָה יְתָאֳרֵהוּ
sources.says: Rashi says it means turning in a curve, as in Isaiah 'he marks it out with a compass'.

sources.quote: ענין הקפה וסבוב, כמו (ישעיהו מד יג) ובמחוגה יתארהו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means going around, as in the same verse in Isaiah.

15:15.headline: The new name Devir means 'book', just like the old one
15:15.body: The verse says Devir was once called Kiryat Sefer, 'town of the book'. Radak cites the sages that in Persian a book is called devir.

sources.quote: ארז״ל כי בלשון פרסי קוראין דביר לספר
sources.says: Radak says the sages taught that in Persian a book is called devir.

15:15.headline: The 'town of the book' hints at laws Othniel won back
15:15.body: Rashi brings the sages' reading of the name Kiryat Sefer. It stands for laws forgotten while Israel mourned Moses, which Othniel son of Kenaz recovered by his own reasoning.

sources.quote: אֵלּוּ הֲלָכוֹת שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּכְּחוּ בִּימֵי אֶבְלוֹ שֶׁל משֶׁה שֶׁהֶחֱזִיר עָתְנִיאֵל בֵּן קְנַז מִפִּלְפּוּלוֹ
sources.says: Rashi cites the sages: these are laws forgotten during the mourning for Moses, which Othniel son of Kenaz restored through his reasoning.

15:17.headline: Caleb's brother has a different father's name
15:17.body: Caleb is son of Yefuneh, but Othniel is son of Kenaz. Rashi says they were brothers through their mother, while Radak thinks Kenaz was the head of the family both belonged to.

sources.quote: אֲחִי כָלֵב מֵאִמּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says he was Caleb's brother through their mother.

sources.quote: והנכון אצלי עוד כי קנז היה שם ראש המשפחה והתיחסו בני המשפחה אליו
sources.says: Radak says the better view is that Kenaz was the name of the family's head, and the family members traced themselves to him.

15:18.headline: She urges him to ask, but she ends up asking
15:18.body: Achsah urges her husband to ask her father for a field, yet she makes the request herself. Radak says he refused to ask, while Metzudat David says she got his permission to ask herself.

sources.quote: הסיתה בעלה לשאול מאת אביה שדה ולא רצה הוא לשאול
sources.says: Radak says she urged her husband to ask her father for a field, and he did not want to ask.

sources.quote: הסיתה את בעלה ופתתה אותו לתת לה רשות שתשאל היא שדה מאביה
sources.says: Metzudat David says she persuaded her husband to give her permission to ask her father for a field herself.

15:19.headline: Negev means the south, and also dry land
15:19.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion read נגב here as dry ground with no water, from the word for drying up. Targum Jonathan, as Radak notes, reads it as 'the land of the south'.

sources.quote: אֶרֶץ הַנֶּגֶב חֲרֵבָה
sources.says: Rashi says the land of the Negev means a dry land.

sources.quote: ענין יובש, כמו (ישעיהו כא א) כסופות בנגב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means dryness.

sources.quote: ויונתן תרגם ארץ הנגב ארי לארע דרומה יהבתני
sources.says: Radak notes that Targum Jonathan renders it 'you have given me a land of the south'.

15:21.headline: Joshua listed only the towns standing on the borders
15:21.body: מקצה means 'at the edge'. Rashi and Radak cite the sages: Joshua counted only the towns that stood on the borders.

sources.quote: לֹא מָנָה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אֶלָּא עֲיָירוֹת הָעוֹמְדוֹת עַל הַגְּבוּלִים
sources.says: Rashi cites the sages that Joshua listed only towns standing on the borders.

sources.quote: לא מנה יהושע אלא הערים העומדות על הגבולים
sources.says: Radak says the word 'at the edge' matches the sages' teaching that Joshua listed only border towns.

15:22.headline: The sages hear a lesson about silence in three town names
15:22.body: Kinah, Dimonah and Adadah sound like 'grievance', 'silent' and 'forever'. The Talmud, cited by Malbim, reads them: whoever has a grievance against his fellow and stays silent, the One who dwells forever will judge for him.

sources.quote: כל מי שי״ל קנאה על חברו ודומם שוכן עדי עד עושה לו דין
sources.says: Malbim cites the Talmud: whoever has a grievance against his fellow and stays silent, He who dwells forever will do him justice.

15:31.headline: Ziklag, Madmannah and Sansannah read as a second lesson
15:31.body: The Talmud, cited by Malbim, hears 'cry over a mouthful', 'silent' and 'bush' in these names. Whoever has cause to cry out over his food against his fellow and stays silent, He who dwells in the bush will judge for him.

sources.quote: כל מי שי״ל צעקת לגימא על חברו ודומם שוכן בסנה עושה לו דין
sources.says: Malbim cites the Talmud: whoever has a cry over food against his fellow and stays silent, He who dwells in the bush will do him justice.

15:47.headline: 'And border' after the sea means its islands
15:47.body: The verse ends 'the Great Sea and border'. Rashi says the extra word means the islands in the sea, and Metzudat David says they too count as Judah's land.

sources.quote: וּגְבוּל נִסִּין שֶׁבַּיָּם
sources.says: Rashi says 'and border' means the islands in the sea.

sources.quote: גם גבול הים הם האיים אשר בים, אף הם לנחלת יהודה יחשבו
sources.says: Metzudat David says the border of the sea is its islands, and they count as Judah's inheritance.

15:63.headline: Written 'will not be able', read 'could not'
15:63.body: It is written יוכלו, 'will not be able', but read יכלו, 'could not'. Radak says the written form hints that they would not succeed until David came.

sources.quote: כתיב יוכלו כי אף בזמן העתיד לא יוכלו עד שיבא דוד וקרי יכלו כי לא יכלו אז להורישם
sources.says: Radak says it is written 'will not be able' because even later they could not until David came, and read 'could not' for the time of the conquest.

15:63.headline: The sages say these Jebusites were Philistines, protected by an oath
15:63.body: Rashi brings a view that Judah could have driven them out, but Abraham's oath to Abimelech held them back. These 'Jebusites' were Philistines, named for a tower (Rashi) or a man (Radak) called Jebus.

sources.quote: יְכוֹלִין הָיוּ, אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ רַשָּׁאִין מֵחֲמַת הַשְּׁבוּעָה שֶׁנִּשְׁבַּע אַבְרָהָם לַאֲבִימֶלֶךְ
sources.says: Rashi cites the Sifrei: they were able, but were not permitted because of the oath Abraham swore to Abimelech.

sources.quote: וִיבוּסִי זֶה לֹא עַל שֵׁם הָאוּמָּה הָיָה, אֶלָּא מִגְדַּל דָּוִד שֶׁהָיָה בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם וּשְׁמוֹ יְבוּס
sources.says: Rashi says this Jebusite is not named for the nation but for a tower in Jerusalem called Jebus, whose people were Philistines.

sources.quote: והיבוסי הזה לא היה היבוסי משבעה גוים אלא אדם אחד שהיה שמו יבוס והיה מפלשתים מזרע אבימלך
sources.says: Radak says this Jebusite was not one of the seven nations but a man named Jebus, a Philistine of Abimelech's line.

24:3.headline: Written without its last letter, 'I multiplied' hints at 'strife'
24:3.body: The word is read וארבה, 'I multiplied his seed', but it is written without the final ה. Rashi and Radak hear ריב, 'strife', in the written form: God tested Abraham many times before giving him a son.

sources.quote: כַּמָּה מְרִיבוֹת וְנִסְיוֹנוֹת עָשִׂיתִי עִמּוֹ, עַד שֶׁלֹּא נָתַתִּי לוֹ זֶרַע
sources.says: Rashi says the missing ה points to how many quarrels and trials God brought on Abraham before giving him children.

sources.quote: הכתוב הוא לשון ריב ומסה כלומר הרבה נסיונות נסיתיו ועמד בכלם
sources.says: Radak says the written form means strife and testing: God tested Abraham many times and he stood up to all of them.

24:7.headline: A darkness that blocks the light, not just the dark
24:7.body: מאפל appears only here. It comes from אופל, 'darkness'. Malbim says this form means the thing that makes dark: the cloud that blinded the Egyptians while Israel had light.

sources.quote: מאפל. מלשון אופל וחושך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from אופל, darkness.

sources.quote: ושם מאפל נבדל משם אופל, שבא על דבר המאפיל ומכסה את האור, שהוא הענן והחשך שהיה מאפיל בפני המצרים ויאר את הלילה לישראל
sources.says: Malbim says מאפל differs from אופל: it means the thing that darkens and covers the light, the cloud that darkened Egypt's way and lit the night for Israel.

24:12.headline: The 'hornet': a real stinging insect, or the panic news brought?
24:12.body: Radak and Metzudat Zion follow the sages: a real insect that stung the enemy and blinded them. Malbim reads it as a picture: the news that God beat two Amorite kings for Israel stung like a hornet, and the Girgashites fled.

sources.quote: שהוא מין שרץ עוף, שהטילה בהם ארס
sources.says: Metzudat Zion cites the sages: it is a kind of flying insect that shot venom into them.

sources.quote: והצרעה היא מין זבוב רע מטיל ארס ואמרו כי היתה הצרעה מכה בעיניה ומסמא עיניהם
sources.says: Radak says it is a harmful fly that injects venom, and the sages said it struck the enemy's eyes and blinded them.

sources.quote: השמועה ששמע שכבשת שני מלכי האמורי לא בחרבך ולא בקשתך רק ע"י ישועת ה' זאת היה כצרעה
sources.says: Malbim says the report that Israel beat the two Amorite kings by God's help, not by sword or bow, was itself the hornet, and the people fled in fear.

24:19.headline: Why 'holy' is plural when it describes one God
24:19.body: The verse says אלהים קדשים, literally 'holy ones'. Rashi says Hebrew often puts words of lordship in the plural, as Joseph alone is called 'the lords of the land'. Radak calls it a plural of honor.

sources.quote: בְּרוֹב מְקוֹמוֹת נִקְרָא כָּל לְשׁוֹן רַבָּנוּת לְשׁוֹן רַבִּים
sources.says: Rashi says that in many places words of lordship are put in the plural, because this name is a title of rule.

sources.quote: קדושים לשון תפארת כמו אלהים
sources.says: Radak says the plural קדושים is a form of glory, like the plural word אלהים itself.

24:22.headline: Who are the witnesses 'in you'? Yourselves, or your soul and body
24:22.body: Joshua says עדים אתם בכם, 'you are witnesses in you'. Radak's plain reading: you yourselves testify against yourselves. He also brings a reading that the witnesses are the soul, which comes from heaven, and the body, which comes from the earth.

sources.quote: אתם בעצמכם תהיו עדים בכם כי אתם בחרתם לכם את ה' ויש מפרשים עדים אתם בכם הנשמה והגוף
sources.says: Radak says you yourselves will be witnesses that you chose God, and notes that some explain the witnesses as the soul and the body.

24:26.headline: 'Under the oak' or 'under the doorpost'?
24:26.body: האלה usually means a large tree. Targum Jonathan renders it אלתא, which Rashi explains as the doorposts of the entrance. Others say it is the tree at Shechem where Jacob buried the foreign idols.

sources.quote: תְּחוֹת אַלְּתָא, הִיא מְזוּזוֹת הַפֶּתַח
sources.says: Rashi quotes the Targum, 'under the אלתא', and says it means the doorposts of the entrance; he also brings the view that it is the tree at Shechem.

sources.quote: ובמדרש כי היא האלה שטמן תחתיה יעקב אלהי הנכר
sources.says: Radak says the midrash takes it as the tree under which Jacob buried the foreign gods, while the Targum took it as the doorpost of the gate.

24:26.headline: Shechem is called a 'sanctuary' because the Ark was there
24:26.body: There was no Temple at Shechem. Rashi, Radak and Metzudat David say the place is called מקדש, 'sanctuary', because the Ark was brought there for the covenant.

sources.quote: הבית שהיה שם הארון בשכם קראו מקדש לקדושת הארון שהיה שם לשעה
sources.says: Radak says the house in Shechem where the Ark stood is called a sanctuary because of the Ark's holiness, for that time only.

sources.quote: היא שכם, ולשעתו קראו מקדש, לפי שהיה שם הארון
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is Shechem, called a sanctuary for that moment because the Ark was there.

24:27.headline: How can a stone 'hear'?
24:27.body: Joshua says the stone 'heard' all of God's words. Rashi first gives the Targum, which makes it a stone like the two tablets, with words written on it. Rashi also allows the plain sense, and Metzudat David says it is as if the stone heard, since the words were spoken in that place.

sources.quote: וְגַם יֵשׁ לְפוֹתְרוֹ כְּמַשְׁמָעוֹ, כִּי הִיא שָׁמְעָה אֶת הַדְּבָרִים אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּרְתִּי לָכֶם
sources.says: Rashi gives the Targum's reading of a stone like the two tablets of the covenant, then says it can also be read plainly: the stone heard the words Joshua spoke.

sources.quote: רצה לומר, במקום הזה נאמר, וכאלו שמעה היא
sources.says: Metzudat David says the words were said in this place, so it is as if the stone heard them.

24:30.headline: Timnat Serah, also called Timnat Heres: two names, two stories
24:30.body: Judges calls the town תמנת חרס. Rashi says חרס, 'sun', recalls a sun image set on the grave of Joshua, who made the sun stand still. Or its name was Heres, and it was called סרח, 'rotting', because its fruit was so rich it spoiled.

sources.quote: עַל שֵׁם שֶׁהֶעֱמִידוּ תְּמוּנַת הַחַמָּה עַל קִבְרוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it is called Timnat Heres because they set an image of the sun on Joshua's grave; others say its fruit rotted from richness, so it was called Serah.

sources.quote: ולמה נקרא שמה סרח שהיו פירותיה מסריחין מרוב שמנן
sources.says: Radak says both names are one place, with letters swapped, and brings the view that it was called Serah because its fruit rotted from its richness.

24:30.headline: Mount Gaash: the mountain that shook at Joshua's burial
24:30.body: The sages found no other mountain named געש. They read the name as 'quaking': the mountain shook against Israel because they did not mourn Joshua properly.

sources.quote: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁרָעַשׁ עֲלֵיהֶם הָהָר לְהוֹרְגָם
sources.says: Rashi says the mountain shook over them to kill them, because they did not eulogize Joshua as they should.

sources.quote: חזרנו על המקרא ולא מצאנו מקום ששמו הר געש
sources.says: Radak cites the sages: they searched Scripture and found no place called Mount Gaash, so they read it as the mountain that quaked on the day of his burial.

24:31.headline: The elders lengthened their 'days', not their years
24:31.body: The elders 'lengthened days' after Joshua. Rashi reads the word closely: only days, not years. Their lives were cut short as a punishment.

sources.quote: יָמִים הֶאֱרִיכוּ, שָׁנִים לֹא הֶאֱרִיכוּ, שֶׁנֶּעֶנְשׁוּ
sources.says: Rashi says they lengthened days but not years, because they were punished.

24:32.headline: Joseph comes back to Shechem, the place he was taken from
24:32.body: Rashi says Joseph was stolen from Shechem, so he was buried in Shechem. Radak adds that when Jacob gave Joseph 'one שכם', one portion, the word already hinted at burial in the city Shechem.

sources.quote: מִשְּׁכֶם גְּנָבוּהוּ, לִשְׁכֶם הֶחֱזִירוּהוּ
sources.says: Rashi says they stole him from Shechem, and to Shechem they returned him.

sources.quote: ולפי דעתי בפסוק ואני נתתי לך שכם אחד על אחיך רמז לו שיקבר שם בשכם
sources.says: Radak says that in his view, Jacob's words 'I give you one שכם above your brothers' hinted that Joseph would be buried in Shechem.

4:6.headline: A 'sign' for those who saw it, a 'memorial' for later
4:6.body: The stones are called both a sign (אות) and a memorial. Malbim says the sign was for the generation that saw the miracle, and the memorial for generations who did not.

sources.quote: האות הוא שיהיה לסימן אל דור הזה, והזכרון הוא שיזכרוהו לדור אחרון
sources.says: Malbim says the sign is a mark for this generation, and the memorial is so later generations remember.

sources.quote: באו האבנים שלוקחו מתחת מצב רגלי הכהנים נושאי הארון, לאות שנקרע הירדן בכח הארון
sources.says: Malbim says the stones from under the priests' feet show that the Jordan split by the power of the ark.

4:9.headline: תחת: not 'under' their feet, but 'in the place' they stood
4:9.body: תחת usually means 'under'. Radak and Metzudat Zion read it here as 'in the place of', since the priests had not yet moved when the stones were set.

sources.quote: תחת מצב. מקום מצב לא תחת רגליהם שהרי לא זזו משם עד שנעשה כל מה שהיה להם לעשות
sources.says: Radak says it means the place where they stood, not under their feet, since they did not move until everything was done.

sources.quote: תחת. במקום
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says תחת here means 'in the place of'.

4:9.headline: 'To this day' means forever, whenever you read it
4:9.body: Metzudat David says 'until this day' means for all time. Whoever reads the verse, in any age, says 'this day' about his own day.

sources.quote: עד היום הזה רצה לומר, עד עולם, כי כל קורא הפסוק הזה בזמנו, אומר עד היום הזה, והוא כלל גדול בדברי הנביאים
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means forever, because each reader says 'this day' in his own time, and calls this a great rule in the prophets.

4:12.headline: חמשים: armed men, named for marching in fifties
4:12.body: חמשים means armed for battle, and the Targum renders it 'girded'. Malbim says they got the name because they marched in units of fifty, each with an officer.

sources.quote: ושם חמושים, מצד שהיה דרכם להתחלק לגדודים של חמשים חמשים איש ושר חמשים בראשם
sources.says: Malbim says they are called חמושים because they divided into troops of fifty men with an officer over each fifty.

sources.quote: מְזָרְזִין קֳדָם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Targum Jonathan translates the word as 'girded', ready for war.

4:13.headline: חלוצים: armed men, or men drawn out from the rest?
4:13.body: Metzudat Zion reads חלוצי as 'armed'. Malbim says they got the name because they were drawn out (נחלצו) from their brothers to go to war, since not all of them went.

sources.quote: חלוצי. מזוין, כמו (דברים ג יח) חלוצים תעברו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means armed, as in 'you shall cross over armed'.

sources.quote: ושם חלוצים על שנחלצו מן יתר אחיהם ללכת למלחמה, כי לא הלכו כולם
sources.says: Malbim says they are called חלוצים because they were drawn out from their brothers to go to war, as not all of them went.

4:16.headline: 'Went up', not 'crossed': which bank did the priests climb?
4:16.body: The verse says the priests 'went up' from the Jordan, not that they 'crossed' it. Rashi learns they climbed back onto the bank they had stood beside, while Malbim says they climbed out on the far side.

sources.quote: וְיַעַבְרוּ' אֵין כְּתִיב כָּאן, אֶלָּא 'וְיַעֲלוּ', לָמַדְנוּ שֶׁעַל הַשָּׂפָה שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹמְדִין אֶצְלָהּ עָלוּ
sources.says: Rashi says the verse says 'went up' and not 'crossed', so they went up onto the bank they had been standing by.

sources.quote: שעלו מן שפת הירדן המערבי אל היבשה, לכן אמר ויעלו לא ויעברו
sources.says: Malbim says they went up from the western edge of the Jordan onto dry land, which is why it says 'went up' and not 'crossed'.

9:4.headline: Did they pose as envoys, or just pack food for the road?
9:4.body: Rashi, Radak and Ralbag read ויצטירו from ציר, an envoy: they dressed up as messengers from far away. The Aramaic Targum reads it with a ד, from צידה, food for the road. Radak is surprised by that.

sources.quote: עָשׂוּ עַצְמָם כְּהוֹלְכִים בִּשְׁלִיחוּת
sources.says: Rashi says they made themselves look like men on a mission, from ציר, envoy.

sources.quote: ומן התימה שתירגם אותו יונתן כמו בדל"ת איזדודו מן צדה
sources.says: Radak says it means they made themselves envoys, and he finds it odd that the Targum read it with a dalet, from provisions.

sources.quote: וְאִזְדַוָדוּ וּנְסִיבוּ
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'they took provisions'.

sources.quote: שהציר הוא ההולך בשליחות להביא מענה בחזרה
sources.says: Malbim says a ציר is a messenger who must bring an answer back.

9:4.headline: Wineskins 'split' or 'tied up'?
9:4.body: Rashi reads ומצררים from Aramaic as 'split open'. Metzudat Zion and Metzudat David read it as 'tied up', like a bundle of money, bound around the cracks.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן מְבוּקָּעִים, לְשׁוֹן אֲרַמִּי
sources.says: Rashi says it means split, from Aramaic.

sources.quote: ומצוררים מקושרים, כמו (בראשית מב לה) צרור כספו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means tied up, like 'his bundle of money'.

sources.quote: מקושרים סביבות הבקיעים
sources.says: Metzudat David says they were tied up around the cracks.

9:5.headline: Their bread was 'spotted': moldy, scorched, or dried to crumbs?
9:5.body: נקדים can mean spotted. Metzudat David and Radak say the bread had gone moldy, with colored spots. Rashi says it was scorched dry, and the Targum calls it hard biscuit. Ralbag says it had crumbled into small pieces.

sources.quote: כי יש בלחם המעופש אדום וירוק ושחור נקודים נקודים
sources.says: Radak says moldy bread has red, green and black spots, and he also gives the Targum's 'biscuit' reading.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן מוֹקֵד, וְכֵן תִּרְגְּמוֹ יוֹנָתָן: כִּסְנִין
sources.says: Rashi says it means burnt, from מוקד, and the Targum renders it biscuits.

sources.quote: הוא הפת היבש שמתפרר מצד יבשו לפירורין דקים
sources.says: Ralbag says it is bread so dry it crumbles into fine pieces.

9:7.headline: The Hivite acted like a snake, which in Aramaic is חויא
9:7.body: Radak cites a midrash on the name החוי, the Hivite. It asks: were they really Hivites? It answers that they acted like a חויא, the Aramaic word for snake, which tricked Eve.

sources.quote: אלא שעשו מעשה חויא פירוש נחש כלומר שרמו את ישראל כמו הנחש שרמה את חוה
sources.says: Radak cites the midrash: they acted like a snake, deceiving Israel as the snake deceived Eve.

9:7.headline: 'Perhaps' here means 'most likely'
9:7.body: Israel says 'perhaps you live among us'. Malbim says אולי is used when a thing is close to true. So Israel was saying it was likely, not just possible, that these men were local.

sources.quote: שגדר מלת אולי הוא במקום שהדבר קרוב שהוא כן ויותר נוטה אל החיוב מאל השלילה
sources.says: Malbim says אולי is used where the thing is likely so, leaning more to yes than no.

9:9.headline: Came 'for God's name': because of His fame, or to join His faith?
9:9.body: Metzudat David says they came because they heard of God's fame. Malbim says they claimed they came to accept God and His Torah. That would explain why a far-off people wanted a covenant.

sources.quote: לשם ה׳. בעבור פרסום שם ה׳
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means because of the fame of God's name.

sources.quote: שאנו רוצים להקים ברית הדת והאמונה לקבל אלהותו ותורתו
sources.says: Malbim says they claimed they wanted a covenant of faith, to accept God and His Torah.

9:14.headline: 'They took' from the food: tasted it, or learned from it?
9:14.body: Radak gives two readings. ויקחו may mean 'they learned', as in לקח, teaching: the dry bread convinced them. Or they really took some food and ate it to seal the pact. Metzudat David gives the same two options.

sources.quote: יש מפרשים אותו כמו למדו מן לקח טוב
sources.says: Radak says some read it as 'they learned', from לקח, teaching, and he also gives the plain reading that they ate.

sources.quote: לקחו מופת וראייה מיובש צידם והאמינו להם, או לקחו מצידם ואכלו, לקיים ברית ואהבה
sources.says: Metzudat David says they took the dry food as proof and believed them, or they ate from it to seal a pact.

9:14.headline: Their 'provisions', or how they hunted Israel with words
9:14.body: צידם means their food for the road. Rashi also hears the verb for hunting in it: the Gibeonites trapped Israel with their words. The Targum says Israel 'accepted their words'.

sources.quote: קִבְּלוּ דִּבְרֵיהֶם, שֶׁצָּדוּם בְּפִיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says they accepted their words, because the Gibeonites hunted them with their mouths.

sources.quote: וְקַבִּילוּ גַבְרַיָא לְפִּתְגָמֵיהוֹן
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'the men accepted their words'.
